name: Boomke Wies
description: Boomke Wies is a Belgian Whist game for four players in fixed partnerships with an auction to determine the trump suit. Players bid a number of tricks (7 to 13) they commit to winning. The highest bidder leads to the first trick and the suit of that lead becomes trump. The special bid 'Boom' (committing to win all 13 tricks) scores 5 points but costs 5 on failure. The game also features 'Meetje' â€” a fallback when no one bids, where the dealer simply chooses trumps and majority of tricks wins 1 point.

Boomke Wies is a Belgian card game from the Whist family, played in fixed partnerships with an auction mechanic. It is distinct from classic Whist through its bidding system, though a simpler non-bidding variant exists that closely mirrors traditional Whist.
4 players in fixed partnerships. Teams determined at start: each player takes a portion of the shuffled deck and shows the bottom card â€” two lowest pair up, two highest pair up.
Standard 52-card deck. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 (high to low).
13 cards each, dealt in batches: either 4-4-5 or 5-4-4 per player. Dealer may choose to shuffle or not. Player to dealer's right cuts.

items.text: Boomke Wies Without Bidding: Simpler version: deal 4-4-4-1 batches, dealer's last card turned face-up as trump. Player left of dealer leads. Each team scores 1 point per trick won. Essentially classic Whist.
